links.title: Ugly milkshake duck
links.note: Rafe Meager, The Universal and the Vacuous Events, 30 Oct 2026 — about 7,000 words, three years in the writing. Read 1 Nov: M's verdict was “fantastic”. Turns the milkshake-duck frame (the thing you love turns out rotten) on X and its owner, then on the author himself: twenty years of living on text social media. Two threads worth the time: a defence of hatred — not as a defect in the hater, but as a functional emotion, with the new-age Jungian reading blamed for the confusion — and a quoted DM that maps five escalating positions, from “I want this, you seem not to, I apologise for my mistake” through “but I know you do” to “there is no you”, which is the ramp to abuse. Ends on politics and the impossibility of separating public existence from it.

links.title: Brick
links.note: A small NFC puck you tap on your phone to block the apps that eat the day — one tap to brick it, one tap to unblock. Physical, so it can't be talked out of like a settings screen can; there are family and organisation versions. Direct-to-consumer Shopify store, so read the marketing with a pinch of salt. Saved 31 Oct 2026 at M's request, still unread.

links.title: How to be more ambitious: a tutorial for humans with models
links.note: Felix Rieseberg (works on Claude) splits ambition into Speed, Altitude, Depth and Range. Altitude: ask for the outcome, not the task — “keep our apps crash-free”, not “fix this crash”; a good sign it applies is when you would otherwise hold meetings about the work. Depth: insist on the instruments real experts use (databases and statistical models, not markdown tables), set an unreasonable target and insist it is reasonable, and make the model adversarially re-derive what you believe from raw data. Not model-specific.

links.title: LibrePaper
links.note: Collaborative writing in HTML, LaTeX, Typst, Markdown, Quarto and Calepin: real-time cursors, threaded comments, tracked changes, version history. MIT and self-hostable, and it brings your own AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, opencode) into the document rather than selling you one. Free tier is limited by storage.

links.title: Bead Me Up, Scotty
links.note: Human-facing viewer and editor for Beads — Steve Yegge’s Dolt-backed graph issue tracker built for AI agents. Saved 26 Oct 2026, still unread.
